description.p: Lambdock is a Wayland-native desktop dock for GNU/Linux, in the spirit of Cairo-Dock, Plank and the macOS Dock. It is built with GTK4 and gtk4-layer-shell, and can be themed, extended and reconfigured live with GNU Guile Scheme.

ul.li: Dynamic window tracking via the Wayland foreign-toplevel protocol
Multi-monitor support and multiple dock instances
GTK CSS themes and configurable application launchers
Dynamic widgets for CPU, RAM, temperature and more
An embedded Guile runtime with hot-reloading and an optional REPL

description.p: Lambdock is now licensed under the MIT License, and every source file says so. Stacks no longer offer the fan view: the icon grid and the list remain, and a settings file that still asks for the fan reads back as the grid. Under the hood the C side was rebuilt around explicit models -- the launchpad, the preferences window and the set of active docks -- with their arithmetic and filtering moved into pure functions that are tested without a display.

The launchpad shows one tile per application again: desktop files that describe the same program, such as the distro package and the Flatpak export of it, are collapsed. A tile whose application is installed more than once offers which copy to start from its context menu, with where each copy comes from and the command it runs. The backdrop is denser, so the labels read over a busy desktop.
The right-click menu of a dock item now carries actions that fit the application: browsers get New Window and New Private Window, and a running music player gets playback controls over MPRIS.
The container image builds again: the Dockerfile now ships the desktop entry and AppStream metadata the build needs.
Keyboard and screen-reader accessibility with a reduce-motion setting, a rebuilt stack fan that shows live file thumbnails, a configurable launchpad, and a roomier preferences window.
Expanded test coverage and packaging improvements.
Improved RPM packaging and stability fixes.
Added Podman/Docker builds and improved APT and RPM packaging.
